m:jelacic: Free to walk, at any hour. The square comes alive in the evening and at weekends; during Advent (28 November 2026 to 7 January 2027) it's full of stalls and people.
m:dolac: The outdoor stalls are open in the morning, normally until 2pm Monday to Saturday and until 1pm on Sunday (hours from guides, to be confirmed: sources disagree on opening, between 6 and 7am). In the afternoon the market is empty: best to come early.
m:cathedral: Entry is free (donations welcome). Visiting hours from guides: Monday–Saturday 10am–5pm, Sunday 1–5pm, but the church closes during services, so check the times (to be confirmed). The spires can be seen from all over the city.
m:tkalcic: Free to walk. Bars open in the morning and stay open until late; at weekends the evenings are crowded.
m:stone: The gate and the square can be seen for free at any hour. The inside of St Mark's Church can normally only be visited during services: the roof is easy to see from outside (from guides, to be confirmed).
m:broken: From the museum's website: open every day from 9am to 9pm from October to May (last entry 8:30pm), from 9am to 10pm in summer. Adult ticket €9, students, pensioners over 65 and people with disabilities €7. Closed on All Saints' Day (1 November), Christmas, New Year's Day and Easter; on 31 December it opens from 10am to 6pm.
m:lotr: For the tower guides give €3–4 and hours around 10am–8pm (different sources, to be confirmed). The funicular runs about every 10 minutes between 6:30am and 10pm, and the ride takes about a minute: it costs less than €1 (from guides, the ZET ticket isn't valid: to be confirmed).
m:gric: According to guides it's open every day from 9am to 9pm and entry is free (to be confirmed: the information is from a secondary source).
m:mirogoj: Entry is free. Hours from guides: April to October 6am–8pm, November to March 7:30am–6pm (to be confirmed on gradskagroblja.hr). To get there, take ZET bus 106 from Kaptol, in front of the cathedral, in about 10 minutes (from guides, to be confirmed). Around 1 November (All Saints') the cemetery is very crowded and traffic is controlled.
vd:fijaker: A historic tavern since 1848 near Dolac, with Zagreb and Zagorje cooking: štrukli, sarma (cabbage rolls), turkey with mlinci and venison goulash. Simple service and generous portions.
vp:fijaker: A main course is around €15–25 (menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:struk: A small place near Dolac devoted to štrukli, Zagreb's pastry filled with fresh cheese, baked or boiled, also in sweet or truffle versions.
vp:struk: A portion costs about €8–12 (menu not seen). Hours from an online guide (other older listings give different hours): to be confirmed.
vd:vinodol: A restaurant with an inner courtyard a short walk from the main square: Croatian meat and fish dishes, grills, lamb and dishes from the hinterland.
vp:vinodol: A main course is around €18–30 (menu not seen). Hours from an online guide, to be confirmed.
vd:purger: A 1932 tavern between the main square and the railway station: breakfast, lunch and dinner with home-style Croatian dishes, such as sarma, lamb and veal, in a simple setting.
vp:purger: A dish is around €10–20 (menu not seen, 2017 listing). Closed on Sundays according to the listing, to be confirmed.
vd:tiptop: A historic tavern in the Lower Town, once a haunt of poets, with breakfast until 10am, a cheap menu of the day and fish, risotto and pasta dishes.
vp:tiptop: Menu of the day and dishes around €10–18 (2017 listing, menu not seen). Closed on Sundays according to the listing, to be confirmed.
vd:quahwa: A roasters' café with comfy armchairs and a small terrace on Tesla street: filter coffee and latte macchiato in colourful cups, tea and cakes. A good place for breakfast.
vp:quahwa: A coffee costs €2–3.50, a breakfast €5–9 (menu not seen). Hours from two listings that disagree about Monday: to be confirmed.
vd:velvet: An elegant café with two rooms, chandeliers and star-shaped lights, with sweet and savoury snacks, hot and cold drinks. Handy for a stop after a walk in the Lower Town.
vp:velvet: A coffee with a cake is around €6–10 (menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:mundoaka: A street-food place a short walk from the main square: sandwiches and dishes with local and international ingredients, for a quick lunch or dinner at mid-range prices.
vp:mundoaka: A dish is around €10–18 (menu not seen). Closed on Sundays and Mondays according to the listing, to be confirmed.
vd:malimedo: The pub-restaurant of the Medvedgrad brewery, on Tkalčićeva street, with a big terrace: craft beers on tap and Croatian meat dishes, perfect for an unhurried dinner.
vp:malimedo: A dish is around €12–20 and a beer €4–5 (menu not seen). Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:lav: An Upper Town café near St Mark's, with a terrace and outdoor tables: coffee, cakes and a restful stop after the climbs.
vp:lav: A coffee with a cake is around €6–10 (menu not seen). Hours from a 2022 guide, to be confirmed.
cd:mimara: Ante Topić Mimara's private collection, with Raphael and Velázquez.
cd:cittazagabria: The city's history in a convent in the Upper Town.
cd:naive: Naïve paintings by peasant artists, a Croatian tradition.
cd:muo: Furniture, clocks and art objects from the Middle Ages to today.
cd:illusioni: Rooms of optical illusions to photograph.
cd:tesla: A technology museum with a mine and Tesla's laboratories.
cd:zoozagabria: A zoo in Maksimir park, north-east of the centre.
